readings: For each circuit country, take the driver standings at each race held there and average the drivers' season-to-date win counts (`driverStandings.wins` as stored) within each race, then average those per-race figures across the country's races so each race counts equally (ignoring missing values). Treat the simple mean of these country figures (each country counted once) as the overall benchmark and keep the countries strictly above it. Then take the mean figure of those kept countries and keep only the ones strictly above that second mean. For each remaining country, return the country, its average, how far it is above the overall benchmark, and how far it is above the second mean, without rounding.
queries:
WITH race_averages AS (
    SELECT r.raceId, c.country, AVG(ds.wins) AS race_average
    FROM races AS r
    JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId
    JOIN driverStandings AS ds ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
    GROUP BY r.raceId, c.country
),
country_averages AS (
    SELECT country, AVG(race_average) AS country_average
    FROM race_averages
    GROUP BY country
),
overall_benchmark AS (
    SELECT AVG(country_average) AS benchmark
    FROM country_averages
),
above_benchmark AS (
    SELECT ca.country, ca.country_average, ob.benchmark
    FROM country_averages AS ca
    CROSS JOIN overall_benchmark AS ob
    WHERE ca.country_average > ob.benchmark
),
second_benchmark AS (
    SELECT AVG(country_average) AS benchmark
    FROM above_benchmark
)
SELECT
    ab.country,
    ab.country_average,
    ab.country_average - ab.benchmark AS above_overall_benchmark,
    ab.country_average - sb.benchmark AS above_second_mean
FROM above_benchmark AS ab
CROSS JOIN second_benchmark AS sb
WHERE ab.country_average > sb.benchmark
